business_problem: Hellenic Cadastre, responsible for Greece's property records, faced delays and inefficiencies as property transactions required manual processing of paper documents, leaving some citizens waiting months or even years to legally own their property.
solution_summary: Hellenic Cadastre, responsible for Greece's property records, faced delays and inefficiencies as property transactions required manual processing of paper documents, leaving some citizens waiting months or even years to legally own their property. To address this, Hellenic Cadastre built a system that reads and categorizes property contracts, applies legal rules, and provides assessments for approval using Azure OpenAI Service. Today, property transaction assessments take less than 10 minutes instead of hours, reducing costs from 15 euros to 0.11 euros per assessment. The system also enhanced property owners' legal security and boosted the Greek economy by enabling transactions to be completed sooner. Greece's Ministry of Digital Governance oversees digitizing public services for citizens and businesses. The Ministry optimizes and digitizes all sorts of processes, everything from shipping to paying fines.

One manual, time-consuming process that the Ministry decided to streamline was land purchases. Traditionally, a person intending to buy a house had to go to the local registry office with a large stack of documents.
The Ministry introduced these changes carefully and gradually across its offices. "Upskilling staff for AI is the biggest challenge for the public sector," reflects Kyranakis.
Today, 90% of transactions across all local land registry offices are processed online. This gives the Ministry complete transparency.
The system also tracks the cost per assessment. "Right now, the cost of each contract assessment is 0.11 euros, down from 15 euros before adopting Azure OpenAI," he notes.
